subject: accessing initial values when they are random

messages.author: 38e260fc5780b4d6
messages.subject: accessing initial values when they are random
parts:
Hi again,

I have a quick question about initial values. When I use random initialization, is there a way to get access to my initial values? I added a print statement at the very beginning of my model block, but the first parameters values that get printed to screen do not appear in my output samples.csv file. 

Are the first values printed to screen my initial parameter values? Is there a flag that I can use to write these to file? 

Thanks again for all your help!
Andria

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] accessing initial values when they are random
parts:
The values printed out at the beginning using print might be the initial values.  There is not flag to use for saving that.  Even you use the printed values, you still lose some precision. 

In RStan, you can obtain the initial values used using method get_inits on a stanfit object. 

--
Jiqiang

Hi Jiqiang and Andrew,

As for the initial random seeds you are referring to Andrew - are these different than the seed saved in the output file (that can be set using a flag)?

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] accessing initial values when they are random
parts: If a seed isn't specified then one is generated randomly using time and then written to the output file. That way you can recreate the results exactly.
